title: Electronic Equipment Installers and Repairers, Motor Vehicles
description: Install, diagnose, or repair communications, sound, security, or navigation equipment in motor vehicles.

tasks.text: Install equipment and accessories, such as stereos, navigation equipment, communication equipment, and security systems.
Cut openings and drill holes for fixtures and equipment, using electric drills and routers.
Splice wires with knives or cutting pliers, and solder connections to fixtures and equipment.
Run new speaker and electrical cables.
Remove seats, carpeting, and interiors of doors and add sound-absorbing material in empty spaces, reinstalling interior parts.
Build fiberglass or wooden enclosures for sound components, and fit them to automobile dimensions.
Inspect and test electrical or electronic systems to locate and diagnose malfunctions, using visual inspections and testing instruments, such as oscilloscopes and voltmeters.
Diagnose or repair problems with electronic equipment, such as sound, navigation, communication, and security equipment, in motor vehicles.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Confer with customers to determine the nature of malfunctions.

clusters.label: Estimating the Quantifiable Characteristics of Products, Events, or Information

tasks.text: Estimate costs of repairs, based on parts and labor charges.
Replace and clean electrical or electronic components.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Microsoft Word.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Harris Tech X.over Pro, Harris Technologies BassBox, LinearTeam WinISD, True Audio WinSpeakerz.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Installalogy Access Client, MobileToys MAIDXL.
